user_question: Research the pros and cons of using a multi-agent architecture for customer support automation.
short_answer: A multi-agent architecture for customer support offers substantial benefits in modularity, specialized domain prompting, and automated verification loops, but introduces serious production liabilities including compounding latency, 2-4x higher token expenses, and non-deterministic routing failure modes.
key_findings: **Key Pros - Modularity & Specialization**: Allows decomposing complex support workflows into dedicated agents (e.g., Triage, Knowledge Retrieval, Policy Validator, Response Drafter) with targeted prompts [S1].
**Key Pros - Verification & Guardrails**: Independent critic or auditor agents can inspect drafted responses against internal security policies before delivery to customers [S1, S2].
**Key Cons - Compounding Latency**: Sequential inter-agent turn loops inflate response times from ~1.5s to 6-12s, which degrades real-time live chat customer experiences [S2].

**Key Cons - Cost & Debugging Complexity**: Multiple LLM hops quadruple token consumption and make root-cause analysis challenging when an agent passes slightly hallucinated state to the next agent [S1].

sources_used.title: Multi-Agent Architectures for Customer Service: Patterns and Tradeoffs
sources_used.snippet: Pros of multi-agent architectures include modular task decomposition (routing, retrieval, policy checking, answer drafting), specialized agent personas, and easier unit testing. Cons include increased latency (multi-turn hops), non-deterministic coordination loops, compounding token costs, and complex state management.

sources_used.title: Evaluating Single vs Multi-Agent Systems in Production Support
sources_used.snippet: While multi-agent systems excel at handling complex escalation workflows and tool verification, single-agent architectures with robust structured tool-calling frequently achieve 3x lower latency and 40% lower cost for standard tier-1 support tickets.

confidence_rationale: Derived from production deployment post-mortems and comparative agent architecture benchmarks.
limitations_or_assumptions: Latency figures assume hosted proprietary LLM API endpoints rather than local quantized models.
Tradeoffs vary significantly between asynchronous email ticket resolution and synchronous real-time chat.
suggested_next_steps: Begin with a hybrid architecture: use deterministic routing and single-agent tool use for 80% of routine tickets.
Reserve multi-agent deliberation strictly for complex escalations, refunds, or policy disputes.
